successors.name: Ostrogoths
successors.text: Pannonia, from which 'the Huns were driven out' after Nedao (454); the Ostrogoths 'apparently first settled in the Pannonian area of Lake Balaton and Sirmium' (Ostrogoths page); Cliopatria's…

successors.name: Rugiland
successors.text: the Rugii north of the Danube (Cliopatria row 455-489)

successors.name: Kingdom of the Gepids
successors.text: Dacia and the Tisza plain, where Ardaric's Gepids won their independence in 454

successors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
successors.text: 'the most distant part of Scythia Minor', where Ernak's Huns settled under Roman rule after 454

capitals.name: Attila's court (Great Hungarian Plain, site unknown)

ledger.x: 106: the Huns north-west of the Caspian.
370: the Huns cross the Volga and conquer the Alans of the Don.
372: the Bosporan Kingdom's lands pass to the Huns.
373: the Hun shape takes the steppe north and east of the Azov Sea.
376: the Thervingi flee across the Danube and Hun dominance reaches the Carpathians.
395: the great raid through the Caucasus.
407: the Pannonian plain east of the Danube enters the Hun shape.
441: Attila and Bleda's first Balkan war.
451: Attila gathers his vassals; the Germanic belt is drawn as a vassal region.
452: Attila 'withdrew from Italy to his palace across the Danube', 'most likely because of famine and disease in his army'.
454: Nedao; the Germanic subjects break free.
454: the Pannonian plain passes to the Gepids.
455: the western margins leave the Hun shape.

wars.name: Hunnic conquest of the Alans and Goths
wars.outcome: The Alans of the Don submitted c.

wars.name: Hun raid of 395
wars.outcome: A raid: Armenia overrun, Cappadocia pillaged, Antioch threatened; the simultaneous invasion of the Sasanian Empire 'defeated badly during the Persian counterattack'.

wars.name: Uldin's invasion of Thrace
wars.outcome: Castra Martis taken in summer 408; after heavy losses and the Sciri's defection Uldin re-crossed the Danube by 23 March 409.

wars.name: Hunnic war of 441-443 (first Balkan campaign)
wars.outcome: The Danube cities of Illyricum sacked in 441 and Ratiaria and Naissus in 443; the Peace of Anatolius (autumn 443) tripled the tribute to 2,100 Roman pounds a year.

wars.name: Attila's campaign of 447 and the Battle of the Utus
wars.outcome: Hunnic victory; peace in the fall of 447 or in 448 (the Huns page: the tribute agreed in 449): 6,000 pounds of gold up front, 2,100 a year, and a buffer 'five days' journey' deep from Singidunum to Novae left as no man's land inside Roman territory.

wars.name: Attila's invasion of Gaul
wars.outcome: Metz sacked 7 April, Orléans besieged to 14 June, the Catalaunian Plains c.

wars.name: Attila's invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: Aquileia razed after a three-month siege, the Po Valley ravaged, Pope Leo's embassy at the Mincio; Attila withdrew across the Danube, most likely for famine and disease.

wars.name: Battle of Nedao
wars.outcome: 'Germanic victory; End of the Huns rule in Eastern Europe'; 'by the early 460s the Hunnic Empire dissolved' with the Gepids, Rugii, Heruli, Suebi and Ostrogoths independent, later Eastern Roman federates; the Huns under Dengizich moved east to the Pontic…

wars.name: Dengizich's war on the Danube
wars.outcome: Dengizich crossed the frozen Danube in 467, besieged Bassianae c.

certainty.note: A steppe people with no recorded border; the Caspian shape is Cliopatria's placement of 'east of the Volga'.
Steppe and Carpathian-basin frontiers throughout; the Danube is the one sharp line, with the Roman provinces, and the 433 Pannonian cession follows Roman provincial limits.
